study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative models pre-trained on cross-sectional data to evaluate intra-individual longitudinal changes in neuroimaging data

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Warped Bayesian Linear Regression (WBLR) normative model was used as the basis, which was extended to evaluate longitudinal changes via a novel 'z-diff' score.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We utilise the Warped Bayesian Linear Regression normative model [ 3 ] as a basis for our work. ... We derive a novel set of difference (' z-diff ') scores for statistical evaluation of longitudinal change between two measurements

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness and subcortical volumes were modeled using a pre-trained normative model. The study specifically highlights cortical thickness changes in the frontal lobe in patients with schizophrenia.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Specifically, cortical thickness and subcortical volumes were modelled, and the models were validated against a subset of 24,000 participants ... For each subject and visit, we obtained cross-sectional z -score, as well as the underlying values needed for its computation, particularly φ ( y ) and .

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.answer: Age-related: Age; Age-related: Age higher-order; Demographics: Sex; Site/Scanner: Site
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used age (with B-spline basis expansion for non-linear effects), sex, and site (site dummies) as explanatory variables.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: This framework models each image-derived phenotype (IDP) ... as a function of demographic or clinical variables (e.g., age, sex, scanning site) ... To capture non-linear relationships, we use a B-spline basis expansion of the original independent variables x n ... To accommodate site-level effects, we append it with site dummies.
